Descartes Systems Group has launched Descartes Spot, a cloud-based spot-rate platform that automates the process of generating freight quotes for forwarders, the company announced Monday, Nov. 23.
Descartes said its new platform can generate quotes for 90% of customer requests within 30 seconds, compared with traditional quoting processes that can be more time-consuming. The company did not disclose how the figure was calculated.
The platform combines carrier rates, schedules, transit times, fees and surcharges to generate transportation options and pricing. Descartes said the platform pulls in the latest spot rates through application programming interfaces, or APIs, that connect directly to carriers.
Freight forwarders typically gather pricing information from carriers and compare available routes and schedules before preparing customer quotes. That process can involve searching carrier websites, collecting rates manually and working across spreadsheets. In a poll of attendees at a Descartes webinar, described in an Oct. 21 company blog post , 94% said it takes more than five minutes to prepare a quote, half said 10 to 20 minutes and 19% said more than 20. Descartes said the results reflect a selected group of freight forwarding professionals, not a formal industry survey. Digital quoting has been spreading across the industry. Freightos’ 2025 State of Online Freight report found that half of the top forwarders offered instant online quotes, compared with none in 2015.
“Speed and transparency are real competitive differentiators in freight forwarding,” said Henning Voss, vice president of product management at Descartes. “Forwarding is a fast-moving, high-pressure business. Sales teams are under significant strain, and facing huge volumes of requests from customers that require manual, time-consuming work.”
Descartes Spot consolidates those functions into one platform. Users enter an origin and destination port pairing to receive multiple transportation options with corresponding routes, departure schedules, transit times and calculated costs.
The platform also allows users to save, manage, send and track quotes. It includes configurable pricing controls and market benchmarking powered by Xeneta , a freight-rate benchmarking and market intelligence provider.
Descartes Spot is part of the company’s broader broker and forwarder enterprise systems suite, which provides technology for logistics service providers. The company said the platform is intended to let sales teams prepare quotes without relying on operations personnel to manually collect carrier rates and calculate costs.
“Leading freight forwarders are increasingly operating as growth-focused sales organizations, where responsiveness and customer experience play a larger role in winning business,” added Ken Wood, executive vice president of product management at Descartes.
Based in Waterloo, Ontario, Descartes operates the Global Logistics Network, which connects shippers, carriers and logistics service providers. Its technology portfolio includes transportation management through acquired TMS provider TAI , shipment visibility, customs compliance and supply chain data services.
Why this matters Freight forwarders often rely on manual processes to gather carrier rates, compare transportation options and prepare customer quotes. Automating that work could help forwarders respond to customers faster, handle more quote requests and reduce the time employees spend on administrative tasks.
